web_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Refresh Audit & Our Independent Verdict
question: Does Manorama Industries remain a compounder after the Nov 12 leadership transition and Pass 1 forensic findings, and what exact action should new capital and our 135 held shares take in Stage 3?

epigraph.quote: Great compounding stories live in hard-to-copy origin supply chains—but keeping them in a portfolio requires auditing every footnote, every executive handover, and every weekly moving average without nostalgia.
epigraph.author: Research Desk Prologue

web_blocks.html: Manorama Industries Limited (NSE: MANORAMA) is India’s largest maker of exotic tree-borne specialty fats and Cocoa Butter Equivalents (CBE) [14, 19]. It runs a 47,500 MTPA fractionation plant in Birkoni, Chhattisgarh, backed by West African sourcing units [5, 16]. Q2 FY27 sales jumped 41.9% YoY to ₹458.86 crore, with ~85% of growth driven by volume [33, 35]. Plant utilization reached ~85%, and CBE plus stearin hit 75% of sales [33]. PAT rose 51.8% to ₹80.81 crore, while EBITDA margin held at 25.8% despite ~140 bps of ocean-freight drag [33, 35]. CRISIL also confirmed zero deviations in the ₹500 crore QIP proceeds [35]. Our business grade stays COMPOUNDER_PASS with kpi_health = PASS_WITH_WATCH.

Pass 1 also flagged a major November 12, 2026 leadership shift [32]. Founders Ashish Ramesh Saraf (formerly Chairman & MD) and Vinita Ashish Saraf (formerly Vice Chairperson & WTD) stepped off the Board into non-board President roles [32]. Deep Saraf became Managing Director, and Mudit Kumar Singh became Chairman [32]. We also patched three blind spots into Chapters 3–6. First, Manorama paid a ₹20.64 crore Customs Section 108 deposit on UAE Palm Mid Fraction imports [36]. It also holds a ₹200 crore FY27 RPT limit with promoter-owned Manorama Africa Limited [36]. Second, raw shea bans in Nigeria and Burkina Faso's CFA 200/kg levy pushed up to ₹350 crore into a Burkina Faso unit [37]. Third, local rivals 3F Industries and AAK India (ILLEXAO EN 10) add real competition [38]. Meanwhile, shares slipped into Stage 3 at ₹1,842.40 (2026-11-23 NSE ledger) and ₹1,859.90 (2026-11-25 live TV) [39].

web_blocks.takeaway: MANORAMA is REJECTED for new capital (VALUATION, TREND) at Stage 3 CMP above capacity-bridged ₹1,800 Base value. For our 135 held shares, we execute TRIM_OVERWEIGHT (sell 45 shares, hold 90 core behind locked ₹1,664.00 daily-close stop).

book_paragraphs: Imagine standing at the edge of a sal forest in Chhattisgarh during the brief six-week summer harvest, watching thousands of tribal collectors gather fallen seeds that most industrial buyers consider too scattered and messy to touch. Follow those seeds into a 47,500-tonne fractionation plant in Birkoni, where they are refined into ultra-pure cocoa butter equivalents that melt at exact human body temperature inside a European chocolate bar. That proprietary origin-to-specialty-fats engine is why Manorama Industries sits in our portfolio—and why we are running a rigorous, zero-nostalgia refresh in late November 2026.

In Pass 1, we stripped away our prior targets and verdicts and re-audited Chapters 1 through 6 against the Q2 FY27 earnings transcript, BSE filings, and forensic footnotes. The core business engine delivered: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue jumped 41.9% year-on-year to ₹458.86 crore (~85% volume-led, ~85% plant utilization, 75% CBE and stearin mix), PAT surged 51.8% to ₹80.81 crore, operating margins held at 25.8% even as global cocoa futures cooled toward $5,300 per tonne and inbound ocean freight trimmed ~140 bps, and CRISIL confirmed zero deviations in the ₹500 crore QIP proceeds. Manorama therefore retains COMPOUNDER_PASS with a PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI flag.

Yet a genuine refresh earns its keep by hunting for what the first draft missed. Pass 1 surfaced a major November 12, 2026 executive transition—founders Ashish Ramesh Saraf (formerly Chairman & MD) and Vinita Ashish Saraf (formerly Vice Chairperson & WTD) stepped off the Board into non-board President roles while veteran executive Deep Saraf became Managing Director and Mudit Kumar Singh became Chairman—alongside three material blind spots now patched directly into Chapters 3 through 6. First, forensic filings reveal a pending ₹20.64 crore Customs Act Section 108 voluntary deposit (July 29, 2026) on UAE Palm Mid Fraction imports under India-UAE CEPA, plus a ₹200 crore FY27 related-party procurement limit with promoter-owned Manorama Africa Limited (whose August 2023 buyout remains pending SPA/RBI completion). Second, 2025–2026 West African raw shea nut export bans in Nigeria and Burkina Faso's May 2026 CFA 200/kg levy explain why Manorama approved up to ₹350 crore for Burkina Faso subsidiary Taang Kaam Industries SA, elevating Sahel capital-at-risk. Third, domestic competition is sharper than distant European conglomerates alone, with privately held 3F Industries Ltd. and AAK India (launching ILLEXAO EN 10) competing directly on Indian soil.

When we opened the market tape and stress-tested capacity math, valuation left no margin of safety. On the verified 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close, Manorama settled at ₹1,842.40 (-14.74% off its ₹2,161 high); on the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot, shares traded at ₹1,859.90 (41.15x TradingView TTM P/E). Technically, the stock slipped from Stage 2 into Stage 3—trading -2.43% below its 50-day SMA (₹1,906.21) and -1.45% below its 10-week EMA (₹1,887.31), with six distribution days in 25 sessions, -20.49% 28-day relative strength, and an unconfirmed 4-hour turn. Worse, once we bridge FY28E revenue strictly to Birkoni's 47,500 MTPA capacity (~90%–95% utilization plus only a partial Q3–Q4 FY28 Solvent Fractionation-3 ramp, ~₹2,050 crore), normalize OPM to 22.5%–23.0% (~₹305 crore FY28E PAT excluding temporary ₹30 crore TTM QIP treasury income), and apply a peer-aligned 35.0x exit P/E (matching Fine Organic's 35.5x), fair value lands at ₹1,700–₹1,850 (Base Target ₹1,800; Bull ₹2,450; Bear ₹1,150; Red Team 30x/20% OPM Bear Stress ₹1,267).

Our independent refresh verdict is therefore strict and unhedged. Because capacity-bridged Base value (₹1,800) sits below live CMP (₹1,859.90) and TradingView's raw support zone (₹1,597.01–₹1,645.65) sits beneath our locked upward-only ₹1,664.00 stop, new capital is REJECTED (TIER_0; VALUATION, TREND). For your 135 held shares in Zerodha (₹1,856.11 avg cost; ₹2,48,724.00 ledger value, -0.74%, 5.83% weight), we execute TRIM_OVERWEIGHT: trim 45 shares (~33%) near ₹1,842–₹1,860 to free ~₹83.7k cash and cut Stage 3 weight to ~3.85%–3.89%, retaining 90 core shares behind our locked ₹1,664.00 daily-close hard stop (cutting open stop risk to 0.41% of NAV). Freed proceeds and marginal cash route 35% to COFORGE, 25% to ZYDUSLIFE, 0% to FINEORG, and 40% to CASH.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The chapters ahead preserve the full ten-year business architecture while integrating every November 2026 forensic patch, capacity-bridged valuation check, Stage 3 trim discipline, and our locked ₹1,664.00 stop. Judge the thesis by the numbers—and never pay 41x earnings in Stage 3 when peer-aligned Base value sits at ₹1,800.
